name: Costa Rica
headline: Costa Rica: +4.6% growth in 2025, −0.1% inflation, debt 60% of GDP
sections: Costa Rica is a $103 billion economy (2025), the world's 76th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +4.6% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $34K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 13.6% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose −0.1% in 2025, in deflation, down from 8.3% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 6.3% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 19.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 60% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 67% in 2020. The general government balance is −3.4% of GDP (2025), a deficit beyond the common 3% benchmark.
The current account balance is −0.6% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 71% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 5.4% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 62% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 81.0 years (2024). Population: 5.4 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
